GB40_QiuXu.additionalInfo: James Mahar GB-40 Qiu Xu is indicated for wrist joint pain that is induced or aggravated by circumduction (circular movement of the wrist). GB-40 Qiu Xu is selected and needled on the contralateral (opposite) side of the affected wrist. This point is typically used as part of a comprehensive protocol, often combined with points such as ST-41 Jie Xi, BL-62 Shen Mai, 77.17 Tian Huang, and 77.22 Ce san, 77.23 Li Ce San Li. While the needles are in situ, the practitioner instructs the patient to actively move the affected wrist. This technique effectively guides Qi through the injured area, accelerating healing and restoring mobility. Point Name Qiu [fil — Hill, mound, or knoll. Xu [it] — Ancient burial ground, ruins, ghost town, or wilderness. Qiu [E] — Hill, mound, or knoll. The character Qiu [ E ] depicts two people standing back-to-back on a hill, with an unobstructed view in all four directions. The character Xu [ ] depicts those same two people standing on a flat, desolate plain; though they look in all directions, they see nothing, signifying an abandoned area. Anatomically, the point is located near the ankle, which resembles a mound. The name of the point conveys the idea of climbing a mountain when one is lost in the wilderness; from the summit, we can regain perspective on where we have been and where we are going. The name describes the point's ability to help a person return to their life's path when they feel they have lost their way.
